title: More Workers Are Using AI — But Many Don't Know Why
paragraphs: AI is becoming more and more common at work. But while businesses are encouraging employees to use AI, many workers don't understand why their company wants them to.
A Culture Amp survey of over 110,000 employees around the world found that many aren't getting the full picture.

While 85% say they're encouraged to experiment with AI at work, only 58% say their leaders have clearly explained why using AI is important for the company. And just 60% say their managers give them examples of how AI could be useful in their work.
Meanwhile, company leaders are actually the top users of AI, with 75% of executives using it once a day or more. But just 53% of regular employees use AI that often.
And the more people use AI, the higher they rate its possible benefits.
So why might companies be struggling to explain to their employees what they want AI to achieve?

One reason may be that business leaders are still trying to understand AI themselves, Culture Amp says. It's not yet clear how AI will change different jobs, and which skills will still be important in the future.
And with company leaders unsure, many managers are still waiting to hear the plan too — so they don't know what to tell their staff.

Culture Amp's Amy Lavoie said that staying quiet isn't the answer, though. Instead, she said leaders should be honest and tell employees that the plan is unfinished. But even if it's unfinished, they should still explain the parts they know!
Employees don't need their leaders to be certain, Lavoie said — they just need their leaders to be honest.
Because when employees aren't told what's going on, Lavoie said, they don't just wait quietly to be told — they probably assume something is wrong!
